Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-

sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Meptazinol, a phenolic opioid, had F 27.9±5.3% in cirrhosis and this was a four-fold increase over controls, implying a non-cirrhotic control F near 7%; this is the most direct threshold-relevant F evidence for a phenolic opioid and supports F<20% for the similarly phenolic morphinan query.

Morphine, a close morphinan analog, is subject to intestinal P-gp efflux (C52,C54,C55) and extensive small-intestinal UGT glucuronidation (C53,C57), providing mechanistic evidence for presystemic loss in the same structural class.

L6 hepatic-clearance records show morphine has substantial hepatic clearance in isolated perfused rat liver (26.0±1.7 mL/min, C66), UGT-mediated intrinsic clearance in recombinant human UGTs (C63,C70,C62), rat liver microsomal glucuronidation activity (C67), and is a UGT2B7 probe substrate (C68); buprenorphine, another morphinan, has human liver microsomal glucuronidation clearance of ~13.9-18.4 mL/min/kg (C60,C61,C64,C65,C69,C71). These support substantial first-pass hepatic metabolism for phenolic morphinans.

L2 records note that cirrhosis increases oral bioavailability of pentazocine, meperidine, and other opioids due to reduced first-pass metabolism (C18,C20), implying these opioids have meaningful first-pass loss under normal conditions.

High-F contexts are either cirrhosis-dependent or not established for the non-cirrhotic query (pentazocine C04/C11, meperidine C07/C13, ciramadol C10) or structurally unrelated (paliperidone C01/C02/C15, haloperidol C08/C14, BI 425809 C09, ACT-1004-1239 C03/C06, UDCA C12); they do not provide affirmative evidence for F>=20% in the non-cirrhotic query.

Samidorphan, a related morphinan, has high Caco-2 A-B Papp (18.77 x 10^-6 cm/s, C48), indicating permeability is not the limiting step, but this does not address first-pass metabolism and does not provide an oral F estimate.
